agreedScope.question: How does a receiving team's play differ on its opening possession versus its later possessions within the same point?
agreedScope.unit: Team possessions within receiving points. Point-start O-line role does not establish unchanged personnel after substitutions.
agreedScope.throwCounts: Keep every actual throw, including centering passes and incomplete attempts. Count attempts ending in goals and turnovers separately; stalls and dropped pulls are not physical throws but may end a possession.
agreedScope.huckTiming: Keep throw 1 separate and examine throws 2–3, 4–6, and 7+ using the original numbering. Do not delete or renumber centering passes.
agreedScope.centeringReview: Review concrete examples; no blanket setup-pass rule or league-wide tactical labels are adopted.
agreedScope.huckOutcomes: Actual catches divided by huck attempts are now compared across first, second, and third-or-later team possessions. Drops are incomplete for this measure and reported separately from drop-credited CPOE.
agreedScope.scoring: Possession goals before another turnover, not eventual point holds. Compare starting locations and retain near-end-zone possessions for scoring.
agreedScope.fieldPosition: Main huck comparison requires a first recorded throwing location at least 40 yards from the attacking goal line, with 30-yard, 50-yard and unrestricted sensitivity checks. Scoring and throw counts retain all locations.
agreedScope.timeouts: Main analysis excludes possessions containing recorded timeouts, without renumbering. A sensitivity check additionally excludes whole points containing timeout or injury markers.
notActive: Average throw distance as an outcome
Forward yards per throw as an outcome
agreedScope.centralHypothesis: Subsequent receiving-team possessions may show more willingness to huck and fewer throws before ending. The study tests the behavior; impatience is a motivating explanation, not a measured variable.

interpretationLimits: Fewer throws means fewer passing actions, not necessarily less elapsed playing time.
A huck may reduce the throws needed to advance, but it can also be followed by more passes or a turnover; the relationship must be measured.
Throws 2–3 and 4–6 describe opportunities among possessions that survived to those throws; they are not automatically comparable initiation stages.
A completed huck and a scored possession are different outcomes.
Use all opening possessions for the scoring baseline, not only opening possessions in points with a later regain.
Starting location, team, opponent, game context and changes in personnel may contribute to differences; observational results cannot identify fatigue or impatience.
Team and league comparisons need uncertainty, game-level dependence and multiple comparisons handled explicitly; team aggregation does not guarantee statistical significance.
The expanded cohort audits zero-throw and period-ending possessions; unknown locations are omitted only from location-restricted or adjusted comparisons.

workingDesign2026_11_11.fieldPosition: Use 60+ yards to the attacking goal line and same-team nearby-location matches as the working direction.
workingDesign2026_11_11.setupRule: Count the opening transfer from a pull receiver as setup when identified. Subsequent handler resets, confirmed brick-start first throws, and first throws after turnover recovery with play continuing are attacking throws. Keep direct attacks after the pull. Record uncertain starts separately; do not delete every opening pass.
workingDesign2026_11_11.matchingAnchor: The existing 510-pair feasibility calculation uses the first recorded attempt location. If a post-setup attack-start location is chosen, eligibility and matching must be recalculated at that location; those 510 pairs are not validated for a post-setup analysis.
workingDesign2026_11_11.denominators: Keep the original physical throws and full-possession scoring outcomes available. A future after-setup analysis must account separately for setup failures instead of silently dropping them.
workingDesign2026_11_11.filmFirst: UFA.tv subscription verified; review actual footage before changing the counting rule.
workingDesign2026_11_11.setupTerminology: Opening setup is the transfer from a pull receiver to the thrower who initiates the offense; it need not move toward the middle. Later handler resets are attacking throws once the initial downfield looks have begun. For a confirmed brick start, count the first pass as attacking. On a subsequent possession after a turnover with play continuing, count the first pass as attacking, even if it is a short transfer inward. A direct attack after the pull needs no separate setup exchange.
workingDesign2026_11_11.classificationScope: Film-confirmed A, C and G: setup on throw 1, attack begins on throw 2. Film-confirmed H and I: no setup, attack begins on throw 1. F remains a preliminary immediate-attack example. No league-wide automatic labeling or statistical recalculation has been performed.

brickStartExpectation.workingRule: A confirmed brick restart begins attacking on the first pass; retain an exception or uncertainty flag if film contradicts that reading.
brickStartExpectation.evidenceLimit: Teddy’s “99%” expresses a strong expectation based on playing experience, not a measured prevalence from this sample.

attackStartComparison.pullTransfer: For a confirmed completed opening setup transfer, attacking throw 1 is recorded throw 2; use the location after setup if comparing attacking starts.
attackStartComparison.brickOrTurnover: For a confirmed brick start or a subsequent possession with play continuing after a turnover, attacking throw 1 is recorded throw 1.
attackStartComparison.directPullAttack: Retain the first pass if the pull receiver attacks directly rather than making an opening setup transfer.
attackStartComparison.preserveOutcomes: Keep full-possession goals, turnovers and physical-throw counts available. Setup failures must remain accounted for; do not condition overall scoring on successful setup.

filmReviewBatch2026_11_12.definition: Opening setup is the first transfer after an in-bounds pull is caught or picked up, when that transfer hands the disc to the player who starts the offense. It need not move toward the middle. If the pull receiver attacks directly, including when the defense prevents an opening transfer, recorded throw 1 is already attacking. After one confirmed setup transfer, all later passes count as attacking, including handler weaves, resets, and passes to an open handler. For a confirmed brick or sideline restart, or a later possession after a turnover, count the first pass as attacking. Bringing a turnover to the goal line or tapping it in does not create a pull setup. A failed setup attempt remains a turnover in the full-possession record; it can have zero attacking throws. Caught-versus-grounded pull handling may be unclear even when setup is clear. A penalty before the first brick-start pass does not turn that pass into setup. Use an uncertain label when the film does not settle the distinction. Opening setup is a working expectation with explicit exceptions, not a reason to remove every opening pass automatically.

timeoutPolicy.status: Adopted by user on 2026-11-12; full-cohort implementation pending
timeoutPolicy.unit: The original receiving-point lineup, followed across its offensive possessions.
timeoutPolicy.rule: Keep completed possessions before a timeout substitution changes the original lineup. Exclude possessions played by replacement players from the original-line comparison; label them not applicable because of substitution, never zero or unsuccessful.
timeoutPolicy.completedBeforeChange: Keep physical throws, identified attacking throws, hucks and the observed goal or turnover from each completed original-line possession.
timeoutPolicy.interruptedPossession: If the lineup changes during a possession, preserve the earlier actions as a partial record. Do not treat that partial record as a completed possession, use it in mean completed-possession length or scoring rate, or attach a later lineup’s goal/turnover to it.
timeoutPolicy.unresolvedOutcome: An eventual hold, break or defensive recovery resolved after the original players are replaced is not applicable to the original-line outcome analysis. Do not recode it as a failed recovery or a break. Preserve the actual receiving-team outcome in the source record.
timeoutPolicy.timeoutWithoutSubstitution: A timeout alone does not establish a new lineup. Flag it separately because rest or tactical changes can still affect behavior; do not silently equate it with a replacement line.
timeoutPolicy.partialSubstitution: For the primary comparison, use the conservative implementation of the same original seven. Flag any recorded substitution, including partial changes. Stop the original-line sequence at its first lineup change; do not resume it by renumbering later possessions.
timeoutPolicy.unknownLineup: Unknown personnel remain unverified; do not assume the original seven continued.
timeoutPolicy.reporting: Report retained complete possessions, interrupted partial possessions and excluded later possessions separately. Explain that later-possession results apply only to original groups that recover the disc and remain on the field.

filmReviewContrastingStarts2026_11_12.setupRule: Opening setup is the first transfer after an in-bounds pull is caught or picked up, when that transfer hands the disc to the player who starts the offense. It need not move toward the middle. If the pull receiver attacks directly, including when the defense prevents an opening transfer, recorded throw 1 is already attacking. After one confirmed setup transfer, all later passes count as attacking, including handler weaves, resets, and passes to an open handler. For a confirmed brick or sideline restart, or a later possession after a turnover, count the first pass as attacking. Bringing a turnover to the goal line or tapping it in does not create a pull setup. A failed setup attempt remains a turnover in the full-possession record; it can have zero attacking throws. Caught-versus-grounded pull handling may be unclear even when setup is clear. A penalty before the first brick-start pass does not turn that pass into setup. Use an uncertain label when the film does not settle the distinction. Opening setup is a working expectation with explicit exceptions, not a reason to remove every opening pass automatically.
filmReviewContrastingStarts2026_11_12.userGuidance: User expects opening pull possessions generally to have a setup transfer and later possessions to have none. Preserve the explicit exceptions already identified in film; do not interpret this expectation as an automatic label for every unreviewed opening.
filmReviewContrastingStarts2026_11_12.nextStep: Freeze the written setup rule for a check on the four reserved games. Film labels for replacement-line possessions can inform that definition even though those possessions are excluded from original-line outcomes.
filmReviewContrastingStarts2026_11_12.methodsParagraph: The comparison follows the lineup that begins each receiving point. Completed possessions before a substitution are retained, while possessions played after that lineup changes are excluded from the original-line comparison and recorded as not applicable. If substitutions occur during a possession, the preceding actions are retained as a partial record and are not treated as a completed possession when calculating possession length or scoring rate. Outcomes resolved only after the original players leave are not assigned to them. Exclusions and their reasons will be reported.

currentCenteringDefinition.source: User clarification in the research chat, 2026-11-13
currentCenteringDefinition.question: Is the first pass a centering pass?
currentCenteringDefinition.target: Separate opening possessions with a completed, clear centering/setup transfer from those without one. The type of non-centering throw is not the target.
currentCenteringDefinition.centeringPass: A completed, clear opening transfer that hands the disc to the player who sets the offense in motion. It need not travel toward the middle. An interception or other incomplete attempt is not a completed centering pass, even if a setup transfer was intended.
currentCenteringDefinition.noCenteringPass: When the pull receiver first looks for a downfield option, finds none and then resets to a handler, that reset is not a centering pass. Other visible first throws without a clear setup transfer are also no centering pass, whether resets, unders or hucks. An intercepted or incomplete opening attempt has no completed centering transfer. This does not establish that the thrower intended to attack rather than set up.
currentCenteringDefinition.cannotTell: The footage or record alignment is insufficient to determine whether a centering pass occurred. Missing evidence is not a negative label.
currentCenteringDefinition.timing: The Houston example describes a downfield search lasting a couple of seconds. This is not a fixed time threshold; recorded event timestamp gaps remain unsuitable for that rule.
currentCenteringDefinition.counting: Subtract exactly one opening throw only for a confirmed, completed centering transfer. Keep every attempted throw, including interceptions and drops, when no such transfer was completed. A one-throw Callahan possession remains one attempt, zero completed passes and a turnover; it must not become a zero-throw possession or be removed. Subsequent possessions receive no deduction. Keep the original starting coordinates.
currentCenteringDefinition.restartRules: The previously adopted brick-coordinate rule and film-confirmed sideline-roller rule remain no-centering cases, with known film/coordinate conflicts preserved. A back-end-line restart is a separate observed context, not an automatic no-centering label from coordinates alone. The Houston user label was based on noncompletion, not a universal rule about back-line starts.
currentCenteringDefinition.compatibility: Keep setup1 and attack1 as existing storage codes. attack1 now displays as No centering pass; it does not imply an immediate, aggressive or downfield throw.
currentCenteringDefinition.automaticLabels: The geometry pilot remains a frozen development diagnostic. This clarification and new film labels do not authorize automatic centering deductions in league metrics.
currentCenteringDefinition.attemptAndOutcome: Where visible, preserve intended setup separately from completion. The user did not settle the precise intended pass in the Houston Callahan example; do not infer intent from its outcome.
currentCenteringDefinition.interpretationLimit: Completed-centering status depends on the result of the first throw. It is suitable for the user-defined completed-transfer count adjustment, but comparing scoring or huck success between these label groups cannot by itself establish a difference in tactical preference. Report all-attempt results alongside adjusted counts; failed opening throws stay in the denominator.
currentCenteringDefinition.versioning: This supersedes the older failed-setup deduction language for future completed-transfer counts. Preserve the original 52 reviews and frozen pilot. Do not silently apply this new target to earlier classifier evaluation or league statistics.

backEndlineRuleSource.interpretation: A pull landing in bounds and rolling out the back is put into play on the back line. This rule does not say whether the next pass is centering.

boundaryExamples.note: The receiver was not covered by his own defender. The thrower’s mark obstructed his initial route, requiring a small maneuver, but the user still identified this as a centering pass.
boundaryExamples.scope: One reviewed borderline example; maneuvering or some nearby defensive pressure alone does not disqualify the opening transfer. Do not automatically label all short contested throws as centering.
